title: Proof of nuclear groebner reduction
html:
Proof. Proof of nuclear groebner reduction

Proof

Uniqueness of the normal form relies on the confluence half of the Gröbner--Shirshov (Diamond Lemma) machinery applied to H_A(q).

  1. The relation set G is a Gröbner--Shirshov basis. The three families — the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1, the braid relation \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i - \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}, and far commutativity \sigma_i\sigma_j - \sigma_j\sigma_i (|i - j| \ge 2) — are closed under composition with respect to the length-lexicographic order. Every overlap ambiguity (\sigma_i^3, the \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1} overlap, and far-commutation triples) reduces to zero. This verifies classical admissibility for the Gröbner--Shirshov basis of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra.

  2. Confluence ensures a path-independent remainder. By the Diamond Lemma [bergman1978], a confluent rewriting system yields a remainder under the division algorithm independent of the reduction path. Thus, r(\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{raw}}(Z, N), G) specifies a unique normal form \mathcal{N}(Z, N) in H_A(q).

  3. Termination. Length-lexicographic order well-orders positive braid monomials. Each rule strictly decreases this order, guaranteeing termination. Combined with confluence, this establishes both existence and uniqueness.

The Lean sibling states nuclear_groebner_reduction and defers the confluence certificate via sorry (-- Ref: [manuscript]). This certificate reduces to the admissible-system machinery already formalised in the unital-Gröbner-bases paper (admissible system). \square
